newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Strong NZ dollar not necessarily bad, says Bolger.
newsitem.headline: Strong NZ dollar not necessarily bad, says Bolger.

text.p: A strong New Zealand dollar was not necessarily a bad thing because it reflected a strong economy, Prime Minister Jim Bolger told a news conference on Tuesday.
Bolger said the New Zealand dollar's value was determined in the international marketplace and the market had determined it was a strong currency.
"In many ways of course we should welcome the fact that the New Zealand dollar is strengthening because it reflects a stronger New Zealand economy," Bolger said.

"It is causing some harm to exporters. They are concerned, they have been concerned about the speed with which the dollar has appreciated and they certainly would like to see it at least stop going up and perhaps ease back.
"Those are is going to be issues of an open economy in any country in the world," he said.
